difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a field K and a K-algebra A and asserts the existence of a maximal weakly etale K-subalgebra B_max of A (source lines 30891-30895). The proof is a directed-colimit argument. Given two weakly etale K-subalgebras B_1, B_2 of A, the tensor product B_1 tensor_K B_2 is weakly etale over K by the class statement, and so is the image of B_1 tensor_K B_2 -> A, again by the class statement which is closed under quotients (proof lines 30898-30901). Hence the collection of weakly etale K-subalgebras of A is directed (proof lines 30902-30903). Taking the colimit B_max over this directed collection, the characterization statement shows that a filtered colimit of weakly etale algebras is weakly etale, so B_max is weakly etale over K (proof lines 30903-30905). The image of B_max -> A is then weakly etale over K by the preceding lemma (proof lines 30906-30907). It follows that this image belongs to the collection and hence the collection has a maximal element, which is the image and equals B_max (proof lines 30908-30909). The non-routine content is the recognition that the union-of-two-subalgebras operation, which is what directedness requires, is supplied by tensoring over K and taking the image in A.
